extraction.summary: The paper proposes hot NEDE: a finite dark-sector temperature thermally stabilizes the symmetric phase, and cooling removes those corrections so a first-order transition releases false-vacuum energy near recombination. Its Abelian-Higgs working example favors a large-mass/low-temperature, strongly supercooled regime (γ≲1, often γ≈0.024 in the benchmark) where a sizable NEDE fraction can coexist with a cold, subdominant dark-radiation bath. The mechanism and background scaling are developed analytically, and the authors sketch interacting dark matter/radiation, inverse-seesaw neutrino mass generation, and a dark-electroweak completion. This is a proposal and effective-model analysis, not a fitted hot-NEDE cosmological solution: the temperature-triggered perturbation amplitude, post-transition stress-energy closure, detailed particle/Boltzmann evolution, and updated inference are explicitly left open.

ideas.title: Thermal corrections trigger a first-order NEDE transition
ideas.description: In hot NEDE, the dark-sector bath restores the symmetry at early times. As its temperature falls through the critical scale, thermal stabilization subsides and the scalar tunnels to the broken phase. This replaces the ultralight zero-temperature trigger field of cold NEDE with dark-temperature evolution. The authors identify this trigger as a new mechanism and explore its background phenomenology; they do not report a hot-NEDE posterior or demonstrate a tension-resolving fit.

equations.definitions: ψ is the NEDE order parameter; T_d is dark temperature; T_◦ is the zero-temperature critical scale; D, E, λ are effective couplings; V₀ is field independent.
equations.domain: Small-mass/high-temperature approximation with the validity conditions in Eq. (III.2); the paper finds this regime is not the preferred strong-transition phenomenology.
equations.confidence: high; checked against HTML MathML and PDF rendering

equations.expression: γ=λ/(4πE⁴)^(1/3); for the Abelian-Higgs example γ=4πλ/g_NEDE⁴
equations.definitions: Dimensionless parameter separating thermal-potential regimes; g_NEDE is the dark gauge coupling.
equations.domain: γ≫1 for the cubic high-temperature approximation; γ≲1 requires the generalized large-mass/low-temperature potential.
equations.confidence: high; checked against HTML MathML and PDF rendering

ideas.title: Strong supercooling permits sizable NEDE in a cold dark sector
ideas.description: The paper extends the thermal potential beyond the high-temperature expansion using a large-mass/low-temperature expression. In that regime, γ≲1 can yield α≫1 and f_NEDE of order 0.1 even when the dark sector is colder than visible radiation. The quoted values are analytic benchmark relations conditioned on the Abelian-Higgs approximation and the stated transition assumptions, not inferred cosmological parameters.

equations.definitions: Dimensionless potential; ψ̄, δ_eff, γ, and V̄_γ are the rescaled field, effective temperature-dependent mass parameter, regime parameter, and potential defined immediately around Eqs. (III.27)-(III.29).
equations.domain: Low-temperature approximation, with γ≲1; thin-wall limit is left for future work.

ideas.title: Percolation and transition duration are estimated in the supercooled regime
ideas.description: The authors estimate the tunneling/percolation condition by S₃/T_d*≈250 and derive a rapid transition for weak gauge coupling. The duration estimate is model- and approximation-dependent; it is not a resolved finite-duration perturbation calculation.
locators: PDF pp. 24-26, especially Fig. 5 and Eq. (III.43)

equations.definitions: S₃ is the three-dimensional Euclidean bounce action; T_d* is dark temperature at transition.
equations.domain: Adopted nucleation/percolation criterion in the analysis, not an observational fit.
equations.confidence: high; text and figure caption checked

equations.expression: H_* β̄⁻¹∼10⁻² g_NEDE², for γ≲1 and g_NEDE≲0.1

equations.confidence: high; checked against HTML MathML and PDF rendering

ideas.title: Hot-trigger perturbations depend on dark-temperature fluctuations
ideas.description: The transition hypersurface is set by dark temperature, so the initial NEDE density perturbation is sourced by δT_d/Ṫ_d rather than the trigger-field fluctuation used in cold NEDE. The authors explicitly postpone checking whether the resulting amplitude and scale dependence match the phenomenologically required initial conditions to a Boltzmann implementation.
locators: PDF pp. 30-31, Eq. (III.49) and surrounding discussion

equations.definitions: δT_d is the dark-temperature perturbation; Ṫ_d is its background time derivative; w_NEDE(t_*) is the post-transition NEDE equation-of-state parameter at transition; H_* is the Hubble rate.
equations.domain: Linear perturbation relation on a constant-temperature transition surface; it does not by itself specify the dark-radiation hierarchy, nucleation noise, finite transition width, or post-transition closure.
equations.confidence: high; checked against HTML MathML and PDF rendering

ideas.title: Two post-transition decay scenarios remain phenomenological
ideas.description: Scenario A deposits energy in colliding bubble-wall fluid/condensate and assumes a time-dependent equation of state, sound speed, and viscosity that the hot model does not derive. The cold-NEDE fit with approximately constant w≈2/3 (reported there near 0.70 with asymmetric uncertainty) is not a hot-NEDE fit. Scenario B transfers energy to particles that later become nonrelativistic and contribute to dark matter; the displayed piecewise background equation of state is illustrative, and the authors state that a full particle/Boltzmann treatment and its perturbations remain necessary.
locators: PDF pp. 31-37, Sec. III C and Fig. 10
ideas.source_figure_note: Figure 10 (PDF p. 34) compares an illustrative cold-NEDE background with prior cold-model fit parameters; it is not a hot-NEDE fit. Scenario B's example uses z_rel=1000, f_NEDE=16.3%, an approximately matched sound-horizon reduction, and x_NEDE≈13% of DM; these are illustrative choices, not posterior constraints.

ideas.title: Dark matter and self-interacting dark radiation can accompany hot NEDE
ideas.description: The proposed (non-)Abelian dark-sector embedding has stable dark matter coupled to dark photons/gluons. Entropy history gives a benchmark ξ≈0.34 after decoupling around 10-100 GeV; the phase transition changes the relativistic degrees of freedom and can heat the remaining dark radiation. A prior NADM analysis is cited for constraints, but this paper does not present a new joint fit of that model with hot NEDE. For N=3, the quoted post-transition ΔN_eff≈0.67 is marginally above the old quoted 95% bound; the authors expect limited impact near equality, an assumption that needs updated inference.
locators: PDF pp. 37-40, Sec. IV A, Eqs. (IV.2)-(IV.4b)

equations.definitions: N_d is the number of massless dark gauge bosons; ξ is the dark-to-visible temperature ratio defined in the text.
equations.domain: Relativistic dark radiation before/after transition with the stated entropy accounting; N_d changes across symmetry breaking.
equations.confidence: high; checked against original PDF rendering

equations.definitions: Γ is the DM-DR drag rate; N_d counts massless dark gauge bosons; α_d is the dark coupling; M_X is the mediator mass; g_rel,d counts relativistic dark-sector degrees of freedom.
equations.domain: Approximate drag scaling in the assumed thermal history; source notes a discontinuity across the transition. The normalization displayed is for one gauge boson before the stated generalization.
equations.confidence: high; square on α_d verified in rendered PDF

ideas.title: The NEDE transition is proposed to generate inverse-seesaw sterile-neutrino masses
ideas.description: A Yukawa interaction with the NEDE order parameter can generate a Majorana mass for sterile states in an inverse-seesaw construction, relating the transition scale to active-neutrino mass generation and addressing an EDE coincidence motivation. The paper's coupling limit is quoted from model-dependent older analyses/random-matrix assumptions; the text notes that newer work weakens it. The eV-sterile branch also depends on mixing, secret interactions, late annihilation and structure constraints. This is not a measured neutrino-mass result or a jointly fitted cosmology.
locators: PDF pp. 40-47, Sec. IV B; especially Eqs. (IV.6), (IV.12), (IV.18)-(IV.19)

equations.expression: g_s Ψ ν_s ν_s generates a sterile-sector Majorana mass after ⟨Ψ⟩≠0
equations.locator: Sec. IV B, Eq. (IV.6), PDF pp. 40-41
equations.definitions: g_s is a Yukawa coupling; Ψ is the symmetry-breaking field; ν_s denotes sterile-neutrino fields.
equations.domain: Schematic inverse-seesaw embedding; detailed particle content and mass/mixing assumptions are model-dependent.
equations.confidence: medium; equation content checked, schematic notation retained

equations.confidence: high for transcription; low as a transferable present constraint without rechecking cited analyses

ideas.title: A dark electroweak model embeds the thermal trigger and neutrino sector
ideas.description: The proposed DEW sector uses SU(2)_D×U(1)_YD, an eV-scale hot-NEDE transition, heavier symmetry breaking, and an inverse-seesaw/approximate-lepton-number structure. It is a construction sketch: thermal and quantum corrections are not fully computed; anomaly cancellation may require additional fields; BBN compatibility depends on dark degrees of freedom and decoupling history. Its parameter example is not a posterior or a validated UV completion.
source_limits: The authors flag possible additional matter for anomaly cancellation.
The quoted BBN temperature-ratio bound ξ<0.2 is conditional on g_rel,d<17 and may be relaxed with heavier/decoupled fields.
Full thermal corrections, field content, and cosmological perturbations remain unverified.

ideas.title: Finite-temperature potential approximations have explicit validity limits
ideas.description: Appendix A derives a one-loop Landau-gauge thermal potential, uses a fitted representation for the thermal integral and ring resummation, and states separate small-mass/high-temperature and large-mass/low-temperature domains. At ψ→0 the perturbative expansion fails when the transverse gauge mode becomes massless; the authors cite an uncertainty of order g⁶T_d⁴ that may affect f_NEDE, while arguing it is negligible for sufficiently weak coupling and a cold dark sector. Preserve this as a theoretical uncertainty, not as a quantified posterior error.
locators: PDF pp. 60-64, Appendix A, especially Eqs. (A.6)-(A.13), Fig. 15

equations.expression: K(a)e^(−a) fit to the thermal integral for 0<a<30 with stated relative error below 4%
equations.locator: Appendix A, Eq. (A.6) and surrounding text, PDF pp. 60-61
equations.definitions: a is the dimensionless mass-to-temperature argument of the thermal integral fit.
equations.domain: Only the stated interval and fit accuracy; not a bound on the full effective-potential or cosmological error.
equations.confidence: medium; fitted expression checked against rendered PDF, full coefficients not transcribed here

caveats: No hot-NEDE cosmological posterior is reported. The authors explore effective-potential/background phenomenology and propose microphysical embeddings.

The temperature-triggered perturbation amplitude in Eq. (III.49) has not been tested in an explicit Boltzmann implementation; transition width, nucleation perturbations, energy conservation, anisotropic stress, and post-transition closure remain unresolved.

Scenario A does not derive the hot model's post-transition w_NEDE(t), sound speed, or viscosity. Scenario B's piecewise equation of state is illustrative and requires full particle and perturbation treatment.

The NADM drag coefficient and ΔN_eff discussion are inherited from prior model work; adding hot NEDE changes thermal and transition history, so updated joint fits are needed. The N=3 post-transition value is marginally above the cited old bound.
Inverse-seesaw coupling limits and BBN constraints are conditional on model-specific particle content and older analyses; the authors flag weaker newer bounds or ways to relax them.
The DEW construction's anomaly cancellation, full field content, quantum/thermal corrections and perturbation implementation remain incomplete.
Appendix A identifies perturbative breakdown near vanishing transverse gauge mass and an order-g⁶T_d⁴ theoretical uncertainty; its impact on f_NEDE is not quantified.
Source inconsistency retained: Fig. 3 visual dotted labels give δ_eff=1.75 for O3/O4, while the caption says dotted δ_eff=0.75. This packet does not guess which is intended.
The paper's Hubble-tension motivation and discussion cite results conditional on datasets and external distance-ladder evidence. They do not establish a present-data resolution of the tension.

usefulness.assessment: High-value mechanism foundation and source of explicit background/perturbation relations; not an accepted cosmological result or executable design.
usefulness.strongest_objection: The key observational discriminator—temperature-triggered initial perturbations and their transfer through a physically closed post-transition fluid—was not implemented. Without that closure, background resemblance or a reduced sound horizon cannot establish CMB/LSS viability or a Hubble-tension solution.
usefulness.bounded_next_test: A source-faithful linear perturbation test should first implement the constant-temperature transition relation (III.49) with the paper's declared thermal history, then compare against a matched-background control while varying the transition surface, finite duration, dark-radiation anisotropic stress/self-interaction, and post-transition closure one at a time. Track acoustic phase, damping-tail response, and matter power. This is a proposal for a later qualified design, not an execution recipe; the necessary microphysics and code support must be established first.
usefulness.readiness: Foundational reading complete; Sol source review and perturbation/Boltzmann closure remain outstanding.
